question_text: Find the angle which the straight line y = √3x − 4 makes with the Y-axis.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say which axis the slope refers to, and what you do to reach the other one.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the angle with the X-axis
steps.margin_note: First mark. The slope of a line is the tangent of the angle it makes with the X-AXIS, so start there even though the question asks about the Y-axis.
lines: The given equation is in the form y = mx + c  ⇒  slope m = √3
⇒ Angle made by the line with the X-axis is θ = 60°

recall.must_convey: That the slope √3 gives tanθ = √3, so the angle with the X-axis is 60°.
accept: the slope is root three so tan theta is root three and theta is sixty degrees
slope equals tan of the angle with the x axis
slope tan theta ki equal, theta sixty
the angle with the X axis is sixty degrees

steps.why: Slope is DEFINED against the X-axis, so any question about the Y-axis has to go through the X-axis angle first.
common_mistakes: Taking tanθ = −4 from the constant term.
Assuming the slope is the angle with whichever axis the question names.

steps.label: Subtract from 90°
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The two axes are at right angles, so the angle with the Y-axis is whatever is left of 90° after the X-axis angle.
lines: The axes are perpendicular, so the two angles add to 90°
∴ Angle made by the line with the Y-axis is 90° − 60°

recall.must_convey: That the angle with the Y-axis is 90° − 60° = 30°.
accept: the two axes are perpendicular so subtract from ninety
the angle with the Y axis is thirty degrees

steps.why: The X and Y axes meet at 90°, so the two angles a line makes with them are complementary.
common_mistakes: Reporting 60° as the answer to the question actually asked.
